booting.text: Come in — give me a second, the desk is still opening.

no_account.text: Come in. Nothing in the vault needs my decision until you have an account — Ines will open one.

lore.text: Come in. Today I'm just decoration — this branch has no manager key on the desk, so go release it yourself at the vault window.

idle.text: Come in. Something in the vault needs a decision? {pending} wire(s) in there.

approve_list.text: Which one? Cooling ones will be refused by the vault, not by me.

cancel_list.text: Which one goes in the shredder?

approved.text: Stamped. Wire #{txId} is released. Balance on your account now {balance} {symbol}.

cancelled.text: Shredded. Wire #{txId} is recalled; nothing left the vault.

limits.text: Over the counter: up to {limit} {symbol}, done in one step. Above that: the vault, {timelock} of cooling, then a release from you or from me. Honest footnote — the limit is this branch's policy, enforced at the counter; the vault clock is the contract's.

why_limits.text: Your session signer could technically sign an over-the-counter slip for any amount to a whitelisted target — the policy cannot read the amount inside the call data. So routing large amounts to the vault is a Teller Desk rule, stated as a partial invariant in our review. What is enforced on chain: who may request, approve and cancel, and that approval waits for releaseTime.

why_manager.text: I hold a runtime role — BRANCH_MANAGER — with permission to approve or cancel time-locked executions on this branch's transfer function. I cannot start a payment for you; I can only decide on one you started. And the vault refuses me before releaseTime just as it refuses you.
